name: prefers-reduced-transparency
plain: OS setting to reduce translucent effects.
meaning: Accessibility and low-vision hint. New and rare.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

safari.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

ios_safari.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

limits.headline: Can tell if you asked your device to make windows less see through
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Check whether reduced transparency is on
Use solid backgrounds instead of frosted ones
Add the answer to a browser fingerprint
limits.reach_label: One yes or no, no prompt
limits.differs: Firefox does not report it. Safari and Chrome do.

story.what_it_is: Tells a page whether you asked your device to cut down on see through effects.

marketing.name: prefers-reduced-transparency
marketing.pitch: Documents a media feature that lets pages use solid colors when the person wants less see through glass.

story.for_you: You never see the check. If you reduced transparency in settings, menus and cards on a site can become solid so text is easier to read.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to keep frosted glass styles readable. It is a very rare signal today, so it has little value for tracking, but it still marks an accessibility setting.

use_cases.example: A web app replaces a blurred glass menu with a solid one for easier reading.
A design tool shows solid panels over a busy canvas for users who asked for less transparency.
A browser game makes its pause menu a solid card instead of a see through overlay.
A video site uses a solid control bar so buttons do not blend into the picture.
A note app drops frosted sidebars so text has a clear background.
A team ignores the value in tracking because it is rare and personal.

legit_uses: Respect OS theme and accessibility needs
abuse: Infer disability or setting for fingerprinting
